d: Works closely with: General Manager, Finance Team, Events, Media, Production

Motivate Events & Media is seeking a highly hands-on and commercially minded Senior Manager – Finance & Business Control to strengthen financial discipline, business performance, internal controls and management accountability across the company.
This is not a purely accounting role and it is not a supervisory-only position.

The successful candidate will be expected to personally review financial information, project profitability, cash flow, receivables, departmental performance and management reporting, while providing the Chairman with independent visibility on the overall health of the business.
The role will work closely with the General Manager and department heads while maintaining direct access to the Chairman for business control, financial oversight and risk escalation.
The objective is to ensure that Motivate is
Profitable by project and business unit
Well monitored against budgets and targets
Capable of identifying issues early and taking corrective action
Review the company’s overall financial position on an ongoing basis.
Monitor bank balances, liquidity and short-term cash requirements.
Review monthly management accounts and ensure that financial reporting is accurate, timely and meaningful.
Monitor accounts receivable, overdue collections and customer credit exposure.
Monitor accounts payable and upcoming commitments.
Review major payments, supplier advances and exceptional expenditures.
Ensure appropriate financial controls and approval procedures are followed.
Monitor payroll, headcount costs and employee-related financial commitments.
Review capital expenditure and significant purchases.
Support audit readiness and ensure appropriate documentation and controls are maintained.
Prepare and maintain an 8–12 week rolling cash-flow forecast.
Monitor expected customer collections and supplier commitments.
Work with management to improve working-capital discipline.
Follow up on overdue receivables and challenge delays in collection.
Ensure management understands the cash impact of commercial decisions.
Coordinate the annual budget process with management.
Monitor actual performance against approved budgets.
Review revenue, gross profit, operating expenses and EBITDA against target.
Maintain rolling forecasts based on current pipeline and confirmed business.
Challenge unrealistic assumptions and unsupported forecasts.
Follow up on agreed corrective actions.
Given the project-based nature of Motivate, project profitability will be a key responsibility.
Review major project budgets before commitment where required.
Monitor quotation margins and expected profitability.
Review project costing, purchasing, manpower and supplier commitments.
Track actual project cost against approved budget.
Identify margin leakage and cost overruns.
Conduct post-project profitability reviews for major projects.
Ensure project managers understand and are accountable for financial performance.
Highlight projects that generate revenue but insufficient profit or cash contribution.
Monitor the financial and operational performance of key business units, including:
Establish clear reporting by business unit showing
Review the profitability of key clients and accounts.
Review major contracts for financial and commercial exposure.
Monitor confirmed revenue and sales pipeline.
Review staffing levels against workload and revenue.
Challenge decisions that negatively affect margin, cash flow or profitability.
Ensure agreed management actions are followed through.
Support the development and enforcement of the company’s authority matrix.
Identify weaknesses in systems, controls and procedures.
Escalate material financial, operational or governance risks directly to the Chairman.
Monitor whether key management decisions and corrective actions are implemented.
Prepare a concise weekly dashboard for the Chairman covering
Participate in monthly management reviews and provide an independent assessment of business performance.
The General Manager remains responsible for running the company and managing day-to-day operations.
The Senior Manager – Finance & Business Control is responsible for independently monitoring, analysing and challenging performance.
The role is not intended to duplicate the General Manager.
It is designed to ensure that
Management is delivering against agreed targets.
We are looking for a strong finance professional who is analytical, commercially aware, disciplined and highly hands-on.
Previous experience in one or more of the following roles is preferred:
Audit / Advisory Manager or Senior Manager
Experience in project-based businesses is highly desirable.
Strong Excel and analytical skills are essential.
ERP and management-reporting experience are highly desirable.
Able to identify problems and propose practical solutions
The candidate must be willing to personally review data, investigate variances and follow issues through to resolution.
r: Improved quality and reliability of financial information
Earlier identification of financial and operational risks
Reduced shareholder involvement in day-to-day monitoring
This is a highly hands-on role.

The successful candidate will be expected to personally analyse financial and operational information, review project profitability, investigate variances, follow up on collections and ensure agreed actions are completed.
This position is best suited to someone who enjoys understanding how a business actually works and using financial information to improve performance.
